titulo: Proposal and scope: four blocks, deliverables and limits
lead: The proposal turns the plan into a commitment. It says what you deliver, what you don't deliver, and what the client needs to do. A clear scope avoids the month 4 fight, when the client thinks "SEO" included everything, up to position 1.
objetivo: write a one-page proposal with the scope in four blocks, deliverables, limits, and what the client needs to do.

aprende.t: The four scope blocks: foundation, content, measurement, AI visibility
A deliverable you can check and a limit in writing
What the client needs to do for it to work
Market ranges as a reference, not as a price list

hero_alt: Two people review a sheet of paper together on a table; one points at an item with a pen.

nos.detalhe: Verified dashboards, a single canonical, sitemap with a real date, robots by purpose, thin pages kept out of the index, entity with @id. Deliverable: an X-ray with no major finding.
A few pages with data that only the client has, a checklist before publishing, internal links. Deliverable: pages live and indexed. The client is the one who supplies the data.
Weekly non-branded export, URL Inspection of the key URLs, a one-page monthly report. Deliverable: the file and the report, every month.

AI bots by purpose, readiness, a monthly question set run by hand, reading of the official dashboards (Bing AI Performance, the AI report in Search Console). Deliverable: the spreadsheet and the reading. Citations can't be guaranteed.

secoes.legenda: Each block has a deliverable the client can check on their own and a limit in writing.

secoes.titulo: How to put the proposal together

texto: Choose the blocks the diagnosis called for. Not every client needs all four in the first month.
For each block: deliverable, deadline, and how to check it.
Write down what you don't promise: position, AI citations, number of articles, indexing time.
Google says there is no shortcut and no special requirement for AI, and AI answers vary with every run. That goes in the text, in those words.
Access to the domain when needed, 1 to 2 hours a week of review while there is content, someone who decides and approves, credentials at the right moment (not before).
Without that, the deadline moves along with their review, and the proposal says so.

passos.sub: a reference, not a price list
texto: US vendors advertise a one-time GEO audit between US$ 500 and US$ 7,500, and monthly support for a small business between US$ 2,000 and US$ 6,000. These are numbers from people who sell, with no independent study.
There is no reliable data for Brazil. Adapt it to your market and test.

exemplo.texto: Price ladder and menu of options are in course 2 of the Selling with AI Program; ranges by service and "price is a test", in course 4.

secoes.sub: Copy it and swap out what's in [brackets].

blocos.conteudo:
PROPOSAL — [client] — [date]

STARTING POINT (from the diagnosis of [date])
- [3 findings, one line each]
- Non-branded searches: [clicks]/[impressions] in 28 days. Questions in the AIs: showed up in [x] of [y].

SCOPE
| block | deliverable | deadline | how you check it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Foundation | X-ray with no major finding | 30 d | before × after report |
| Measurement | weekly export + 1-page monthly report | every month | file and report |
| Content | [3] pages with your data, approved by you | 90 d | indexed URLs |
| AI visibility | question set of [20] questions, by hand, every month | every month | spreadsheet |

NOT INCLUDED / I DON'T PROMISE
- Search engine ranking or AI citation (nobody controls it; Google says there is no shortcut).
- Volume of articles. Site networks. Paid indexer.
- Touching the site or the dashboards without written authorization (attached).

YOU NEED TO PROVIDE
- Read access to Search Console and Bing Webmaster; access to the domain when it's time to verify.
- [1–2] h per week to review and approve content; one person who decides.

INVESTMENT: [amount] — [payment terms]. Scope review on day 30.

secoes.titulo: Practice: the proposal ready to send
secoes.sub: Use the diagnosis and the plan from lessons 2 and 3.

exercicios.texto: Fill in the template with the diagnosis and the plan. Choose only the blocks the diagnosis justifies.
exercicios.pronto: the proposal fits on one page, each chosen block has a deliverable, a deadline and a way to check it, and the starting point has at least one number from the diagnosis.

exercicios.texto: Write the "not included / I don't promise" section and the "you need to provide" section. Read it out loud as if it were for the client.
exercicios.pronto: there are at least 3 limits (ranking, AI citation, volume) and at least 2 client prerequisites, with hours per week written as a number.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: What goes into the "AI visibility" block of the proposal?
opcoes: Bots by purpose, readiness, a monthly question set and reading the official dashboards, without guaranteeing citation.
An llms.txt as the main deliverable.
An AI score from a tool.
perguntas.explica: What you deliver is preparation and measurement. Citation is a result of the AIs, which vary with every run.

perguntas.p: A client asks how much it costs. You saw that US vendors charge from US$ 500 to 7,500 per audit. How do you use that number?
opcoes: Convert it and charge the same.
As a market reference from people who sell it, with no independent study; adapt it to your market and test.
perguntas.explica: These are numbers advertised by vendors, from another country. They help you get a sense of the range, not as a price list.

perguntas.p: Why does the proposal list what the client needs to do?
opcoes: Because content with their own data and domain verification depend on them; without that, the deadline moves along with their review.
perguntas.explica: A written prerequisite avoids the month 4 conversation: "why didn't it go out?" has an answer on paper.

perguntas.p: Which limit should be written in the proposal?
opcoes: "We don't promise search engine ranking or AI citation."
"We use a paid indexer to speed things up."
perguntas.explica: It's the limit that protects both sides. The other three are promises or risky tactics.

itens.texto: Foundation, content, measurement and AI visibility, each with a deliverable and a way to check it.
Ranking and citation are not promised. The client reads this before signing.
Ranges from US vendors (US$ 500 to 7,500 per audit) are only a guide; adapt them to your market.
